question: A tenant installs custom shelving in a rented retail space specifically to display and sell merchandise. Under real property law, this shelving is best classified as a:
choice_a: Trade fixture, which the tenant may remove before the lease ends as long as the premises are restored
choice_b: Fixture that automatically becomes the landlord's property the moment it is installed
choice_c: Emblement, which belongs to whoever harvests it
choice_d: Personal property that can never be attached to real property
explanation: Trade fixtures installed by a tenant for use in a trade or business remain the tenant's personal property and may be removed before the lease expires, provided the tenant repairs any damage from removal -- distinct from ordinary fixtures, which pass with the real estate.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.A (Real property vs. personal property -- fixtures, trade fixtures, emblements), Pearson VUE #094401

question: Which economic characteristic of land describes the fact that no two parcels of real property occupy the exact same location, even if physically identical?
explanation: Area preference, or situs, is the economic characteristic reflecting that a property's unique location drives value, since location cannot be duplicated even for otherwise identical improvements.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.B (economic characteristics: scarcity, modification/improvement, permanence of investment/fixity, area preference/situs), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A city ordinance restricting a parcel to single-family residential use is an exercise of which governmental power?
explanation: Zoning ordinances are a classic exercise of police power -- the government's inherent authority to regulate land use for the health, safety, and general welfare of the public, without requiring compensation to the owner.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.1 (public controls -- police power, eminent domain, taxation, escheat, zoning ordinances), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A subdivision's recorded declaration limits homes to a single story and requires HOA architectural approval before any exterior modification. This is an example of a:
choice_a: Zoning ordinance enforced by the city
choice_d: Covenant, condition, and restriction (CC&R) enforced privately by the homeowners association
explanation: CC&Rs are private land-use controls created by a developer or HOA and recorded against the property; unlike zoning, they are enforced privately (often by the HOA) rather than by a governmental body.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.2 (private controls: CC&Rs, HOAs, easements, licenses, encroachments), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A utility company holds the recorded right to run power lines across a homeowner's back lot line indefinitely, even after the property is sold to new owners. This is an example of a(n):
choice_a: Easement appurtenant or in gross that runs with the land
choice_b: License, which is personal and revocable at will
explanation: A recorded utility easement is a non-possessory property interest that survives a change of ownership, unlike a license (a personal, revocable permission) or an encroachment (an unauthorized intrusion onto another's land).
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.2.b (easements), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A metes-and-bounds legal description of a Texas rural tract would typically begin at which reference point?
choice_b: A point of beginning tied to a monument or established survey corner
choice_c: The nearest lot and block number in a recorded plat
choice_d: The section, township, and range under the rectangular survey system
explanation: Metes-and-bounds descriptions trace a parcel's boundary from a fixed point of beginning, typically tied to a monument or survey marker, using courses (directions) and distances back to that same point -- Texas's predominant land description method given its history of Spanish/Mexican land grant surveys.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.C (legal descriptions -- methods used to describe real property, survey), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A homeowner grows and harvests an annual crop of pecans on the property each year for commercial sale. These pecans, prior to severance, are classified as:
choice_c: Emblements -- cultivated, growing crops treated as personal property
explanation: Emblements are annually cultivated crops that, though physically attached to the land while growing, are legally treated as personal property belonging to the party who planted and tends them.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.A.1 (fixtures, trade fixtures, emblements), Pearson VUE #094401

question: The physical characteristic of land describing that no parcel can be physically moved from one location to another is called:
explanation: Immobility is the physical characteristic reflecting that land, unlike most other assets, cannot be relocated -- a foundational reason real estate markets are inherently local and location-dependent.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.B.2 (physical characteristics -- immobility, indestructibility, non-homogeneity/uniqueness), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A property owner's neighbor builds a fence that is discovered, after a new survey, to extend eighteen inches onto the owner's lot. This unauthorized physical intrusion is called a(n):
explanation: An encroachment is an unauthorized physical intrusion of a structure or improvement onto a neighboring owner's land, typically discovered through a survey, and is distinct from a lawfully granted easement.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.2.c (licenses and encroachments), Pearson VUE #094401

question: The government's power to take private property for public use, provided the owner receives just compensation, is known as:
explanation: Eminent domain (condemnation) allows government or authorized private entities (such as utilities or pipeline companies) to acquire private property for a public use upon payment of just compensation to the owner.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.1.a (police power, eminent domain, taxation, escheat), Pearson VUE #094401

question: If a property owner dies without a will and with no ascertainable heirs, title to the property ultimately passes to the state under the doctrine of:
explanation: Escheat is the governmental power under which property reverts to the state when an owner dies intestate and leaves no legally identifiable heirs, ensuring no parcel remains permanently without a legal owner.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.1.a (police power, eminent domain, taxation, escheat), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A landowner grants a neighbor written permission to walk across a corner of the property to reach a fishing pond, revocable at any time. This arrangement is best described as a:
explanation: A license is a personal, revocable permission to use another's land for a specific purpose; unlike an easement, it does not create a permanent interest in the land and does not run with title.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.D.2.c (licenses and encroachments), Pearson VUE #094401

question: The economic principle that land value can increase through construction of new improvements or renovation of existing ones is captured by which characteristic?
explanation: Modification (improvement) describes land's economic capacity to be altered -- through development, renovation, or demolition -- in ways that change its value, distinguishing it from land's fixed physical characteristics.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.B.1 (economic characteristics -- modification/improvement), Pearson VUE #094401

question: A broker preparing a legal description for a subdivided lot in a platted Texas subdivision would most commonly use which method?
choice_b: Lot and block reference to the recorded plat
choice_d: Informal street-address description with no recorded reference
explanation: For platted subdivisions, the recorded plat map assigns each parcel a lot and block number, and the legal description simply references that lot, block, subdivision name, and the recording information -- the fastest and most common method in developed urban and suburban areas.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.C (legal descriptions), Pearson VUE #094401

question: Because every parcel of real estate differs from every other parcel in at least location, the physical characteristic being described is:
explanation: Non-homogeneity, or uniqueness, means no two parcels of real estate are ever truly identical, which is why courts recognize real property disputes as warranting remedies like specific performance rather than only money damages.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline I.B.2 (physical characteristics -- non-homogeneity/uniqueness), Pearson VUE #094401

question: The rights to the space above a parcel of land, including the right to build upward subject to zoning and aviation limits, are called:
explanation: Air rights are the rights to use, control, and occupy the vertical space above a parcel's surface, commonly bought and sold separately in dense urban areas for development above existing structures.
source_note: National/General Broker Content Outline II.A.5 (air, surface, and sub-surface rights), Pearson VUE #094401
